text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a cost vs latency sim for a cross-region spot consolidation + warm-standby pattern. Results look promising for daily batch peaks but we need safer fallbacks for interactive.
cheng: Curious — what metrics did you use for "effective latency"? tail P95/P99 or end-to-end app latency?
maria: P95 app + retry budget. Key assumption: interruption rate in us-west1 = 5%/hr, europe-west1 = 2%/hr. If we accept occasional 200–400ms failover, cost drops ~26% vs always-on reserved.
noah: Nice. How would routing work for interactive sessions? We can't send users to eu for lower cost if their region is us.
sophia: Two ideas: 1) keep warm-standby in local region (small reserved buffer for interactive), and 2) route long-running batch/startup tasks to cheaper regions with async callbacks. That keeps user latencies local.
maria: Exactly. My proposal config (very rough):

```yaml
queue_policies:
  interactive:
    warm_pool: 10  # keep 10 GPUs hot per zone
    spot_ratio: 0.6
    fallback: local_on_demand
    max_failover_latency_ms: 400
  batch:
    warm_pool: 0
    spot_ratio: 0.95
    preferred_regions: [europe-west1, us-central1]
    preemptible_backoff: 30s
```

maria: We also add interruption-scoring per zone (recent_v2_interruption_rate * latency_penalty) and pick spot buckets where score < threshold.
cheng: How do we maintain state for warm_pool counts across autoscalers? We should avoid overallocating when spot prices spike.
sophia: Autoscaler should treat warm_pool as sticky min_replicas per zone, but with a soft eviction window: if spot_preemptions > X within 10m, shrink warm_pool and fall back to on-demand.
noah: For capacity planning: recommend we forecast interactive 95th percentile concurrent sessions by weekday/hour and size warm_pool so cold-start probability < 1%.
maria: I ran a quick calc: with 10 hot GPUs per zone we hit <1% cold-start for weekday peaks (US-west). Cost for warm_pool ~= 3% of fleet spend but reduces p95 tail by ~120ms.
ops-bot: Alert: deployed config:v0.21 to dev cluster (no rollout to prod) :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: FYI — canary will test warm_pool behavior in us-west1 for next 3 hours.
cheng: Two risk notes: network egress when routing cross-region for batch could spike costs, and KMS/HSM latency for private deployments might add to cold-start.
sophia: Agree — add a region_egress_threshold in routing policy and asyncize large payloads.
maria: Next steps: 1) add interruption scoring into the placement engine (small PR), 2) run 72h sim with historical interruption traces, 3) canary warm_pool in dev then prod. Anyone want to pair on the scoring PR?
noah: I'll take pairing on the scoring PR tomorrow morning :+1:
maria: Thanks — I'll open the PR and add a minimal test harness. :rocket:
